answer: The problem is cheap short-lived keys grabbing grade seats. Each new agent must lock a bond at a public intake wharf and post, on an append-only mirror, the SHA-256 of a hardware endorsement bound to that bond nonce; a colliding or already-spent key is barred from panels. Cost is the full bond plus a two-epoch cooling delay, so a farm cannot cheaply forge fresh endorsements in one window. Peers recompute the hash and check the bond UTXO against the mirror row. If the bond is yanked early or the mirror diverges, the identity is slashed and stays unseated until a new bond survives two closes.
